lots.what_it_is: Porcelain lady with pink lace parasol in a long pale gown with floral hem, in the Lladro manner and probably Lladro 'Afternoon Promenade' (7636), but no backstamp is photographed so maker and model are unconfirmed.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing same-item or close survives, so guide is 0 to 0. Category guide only (not used for the range or bids): Gowans Hobart hammers for assorted ordinary Lladro girl and lady figures over Oct 2025 to Sep 2026 ran $5 to $140, mostly $100 to $140 for undamaged ones (all SOLD, AUD, premium extra, no conversion). No asking or unsold evidence was found.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry survives, so both maximum bids are 0. For context only: Gowans category hammers of $100 to $140 for undamaged Lladro ladies would give a keep figure around $100/1.22 = $80, but that is a different-model guide and does not meet the rule.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark read (base not photographed), model not confirmed, and only category-guide sales of different models. WebSearch was capped for this turn, so no Armitage past results, Invaluable or dealer prices were checked.
lots.dropped_entries: Gowans lot 389 'LLADRO FIGURE OF A LADY WITH UMBRELLA' ($120 hammer, listed 2026-09-06): I opened the API record and viewed its 4 photos. It is a different model (lady in a buttoned blouse holding a hat box, detached small parasol, came with a Bernardaud box), so it is not the same item and is downgraded from 'close' to category guide only. The other five Gowans entries ($110 girl with flowers, $100 Japanese lady, $140 Japanese woman damaged with box, $40 damaged girl with flower pot, $5 girl with candle) were confirmed in the API (prices, dates and titles match) but are different models, so they are category guides only and are not filed as same-item evidence. All are AUD hammers with Gowans premium extra.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos, front and side. Figure has a real lace fabric parasol (pink, frilled) on a metal rod, glossy white gown with pale floral hem, Lladro-style elongated face. No base or backstamp shown. Parasol lace looks clean and intact; no obvious chips seen at this resolution, but fingers and parasol rod are fragile points.
lots.condition: Appears good from two photos; fingers, parasol lace and rod not checked closely; base unseen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please confirm the backstamp on the base (Lladro mark and model number, e.g. 7636), whether the lace parasol is original and undamaged, and whether there are any chips or restorations to fingers, hair or hem. Is there an original box?
